title: The spirometry lab
intro: A spirometer at every bench and a box of cardboard mouthpieces. You'll measure your own lungs, then read the tracings of patients from the pulmonary function lab.

steps.say: "Nose clip on. The test is only as good as the effort, and the effort is only as good as your coaching."
steps.speaker: Sam Ortega, respiratory therapist

choice.prompt: Your partner goes first. As they start to breathe out, you:

options.text: Coach loudly: "Big breath in… and BLAST! Keep going, keep going, keep going!"
options.reply: A smooth curve that plateaus at six seconds: an acceptable effort.

options.text: Stay quiet: "Breathe out whenever you're ready."
options.reply: They stop after two seconds. The curve never plateaus, so the FVC is underestimated.

options.text: Demonstrate once, then let them try without talking.
options.reply: Better, but they stop early on the second try.

choice.lesson: Coach forced maneuvers actively: full effort, and keep going until the curve plateaus

steps.say: Then it's your turn. By the end of six seconds you're seeing stars, and the spirometer prints your curve.
"Now some real ones. Look at the shape before you look at the numbers."
steps.speaker: Sam Ortega, respiratory therapist

steps.caption: Obstruction: a slow, drawn-out curve (a low ratio). Restriction: a small curve that still empties fast (a normal ratio).

steps.say: "Last thing, and the one your patients will thank you for." He hands out placebo inhalers and spacers.
"Check the technique at every visit. It's the cheapest treatment in pulmonary medicine."
steps.speaker: Sam Ortega, respiratory therapist

feedback: "You coach like a pro and read like a fellow."
"Solid. Look at the shape of the curve before the numbers."
"Go back over the normal, obstructive and restrictive shapes: the pattern is everything."
